subject: german
topicName: Cases: Nominative, Accusative, Dative and Genitive

cards.front: Recall a key point about Cases: Nominative, Accusative, Dative and Genitive
cards.back: German has four cases that show the role of a noun in a sentence. Each case affects the articles (der/die/das), adjectives and pronouns.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Cases: Nominative, Accusative, Dative and Genitive
cards.back: Two-way prepositions: movement towards = ACCUSATIVE (Wohin?); location/position = DATIVE (Wo?). "Ich gehe in die Stadt" (acc — movement) vs "Ich bin in der Stadt" (dat — location).

cards.front: What should you know about german exam tips — cases: nominative, accusative, dative and genitive?
cards.back: 1. For Cases: Nominative, Accusative, Dative and Genitive, use a range of vocabulary and complex grammatical structures to access higher marks 2. Check verb tenses, agreements and word order carefully in your written work 3. In translation tasks, translate meaning rather than word-for-word 4. When writing about Cases: Nominative, Accusative, Dative and Genitive, include opinions and justifications, not just descriptions 5. For listening and reading, focus on key words and cognates to extract meaning
durch, für, gegen, ohne, um (e.g. für mich (for me) — accusative)
aus, bei, mit, nach, seit, von, zu, gegenüber (e.g. mit mir (with me) — dative)
während, wegen, trotz, (an)statt (e.g. wegen des Wetters (because of the weather) — genitive)

cards.front: What does Two-way (Akk or Dat) mean?
cards.back: in, an, auf, unter, vor, hinter, neben, über, zwischen (e.g. in die Stadt (acc = movement) / in der Stadt (dat = location))
